case_name: Ladha Shamji Dhanani and Others v State of Gujarat
respondent:
State of Gujarat
Supreme Court of India

11 March 1992
Cr.A. No. 180 of 1980 (From the Judgment and Order Dt. 8/9 January 1980 of the Gujarat High Court in Cr.A. No. 484 of 1977)
The Judgment was delivered by: K. JAYACHANDRA REDDY, J.
1.  The six appellants in this appeal along with 24
facts: The six appellants in this appeal along with 24 others were tried for offences punishable under Sections 147, 148, 342, 353, 435, 440 and 302 read with 149/34 IPC.

It is alleged that these 30 accused who were found in a mob consisting of 300-350 persons armed with weapons like axes, dharias and spears and A-15 among them armed with a gun and A-12 armed with a pipe surrounded a bus on August 5, 1976 at 7 p.m. at village Lalavadar in which the four deceased persons were travelling and set the bus on fire, as a result of which the four deceased persons were burnt to death.
Outside the bus another deceased Surag Bhan was beaten, as a result of which he died.
The trial court acquitted the accused persons holding that the prosecution had failed to prove its case.
The State preferred an appeal before the High Court against the order of acquittal.
issues: Whether the High Court erred in convicting the appellants for their specific overt acts?
Whether the evidence of the interested witnesses has to be scrutinised with great care and caution?
petitioner_arguments: The case arose out of an acute faction and witnesses examined are all interested.
The overt acts attributed to these appellants are not mentioned in the earliest report.
At any rate, the view taken by the Sessions Court is quite reasonable and the High Court in an appeal against their acquittal ought not to have interfered.

False implication cannot be ruled out and that the very fact that A-29 and A-30 who were seriously injured are also attributed a prominent role shows that there was a false implication and therefore the entire evidence has to be rejected.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution case is that all the deceased persons, eyewitnesses and the accused belong to the village Lalavadar which has a population of about 2,500 people.
They belong to two different castes.
One Jattubhai belonging to Kathi caste was detained under MISA and because of the Panchayat election there was enmity between them.
On the day of occurrence i.e. August 5, 1976 in an earlier incident A-29 and A-30 received serious injuries caused by the persons belonging to the opposite party.
court_reasoning: The High Court while disagreeing with the reasons given by the trial court, however, held that only such of those accused to whom specific overt acts are attributed could be convicted for their individual acts.

In a case of this nature false implication cannot be ruled out and that the very fact that A-29 and A-30 who were seriously injured are also attributed a prominent role shows that there was a false implication and therefore the entire evidence has to be rejected.
holding: The High Court convicted A-15 and A-16 under Section 302 read with 34 IPC and sentenced each of them to undergo imprisonment for life.
A-26 was convicted under Section 307 IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 7 years.
Accused 18, 24 and 28 were convicted under Section 326 read with 34 IPC in respect of the injuries caused to Surag Bhan, the deceased and sentenced each of them to undergo R.I. for 7 years.
